Seminar Title:

Existence and multiplicity results for a class of elliptic equations with combined nonlinearities

Abstract:

The primary objective of this thesis is to investigate the existence, uniqueness and multiplicity of weak solutions for several classes of elliptic equations with combined nonlinearities. These problems lie at the intersection of nonlinear analysis, functional analysis, and partial differential equations&mdashfields that are deeply interconnected. Elliptic partial differential equations have applications in various fields of science and engineering, such as reaction-diffusion problems, conservation laws, the thin obstacle problem, crystal dislocation, soft thin films, flow through fractal non-smooth domains, and the elastic properties of fractal media. They are also important in various areas of mathematics, including harmonic analysis, differential geometry, the calculus of variations, and topology. This work focuses on the analysis of elliptic boundary value problems within the framework of Sobolev spaces, generalized Lebesgue-Sobolev spaces, weighted Sobolev spaces, and fractional Sobolev spaces. Quasilin ear problems involving the p(y)&minusLaplace operator are also considered, with relevance to applications such as elasticity, image processing, and electrorheological fluids. The thesis further investigates weighted p&minusLaplacian problems, where weighted Sobolev spaces provide a natural framework for describing spatial heterogeneity, degeneracy, and singular behavior. Such settings are particularly relevant to PDEs arising in nonhomoge neous media and models involving weighted or singular coefficients. The thesis also addresses nonlinear elliptic problems on fractal domains, particularly the Sierpiński gasket, and fractional elliptic equations with nonlocal Neumann boundary conditions. We study the existence and multiplicity of solutions for a class of elliptic equa tions with combined nonlinearities on both regular and fractal domains, subject to Dirichlet, Neumann, and nonlinear boundary conditions. The analysis is carried out within the framework of generalized Sobolev spaces using variational methods, critical point theory, and monotone operator techniques, with the Nehari manifold method, fibering map analysis, and embedding theorems serving as the principal analytical tools.
